data.cultural_impact: The name Amima signifies the close bond and deep respect that Muslims have for the wives of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). They played significant roles in the spread of Islam and supported the early Muslim community with their compassion, wisdom, and patience. The title serves as a reminder of the important role women play in preserving and promoting the teachings of the Prophet within Muslim families and society as a whole.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Amima holds immense spiritual significance, as these women were chosen by Allah to be the wives of His messenger. They dedicated their lives to nurturing their families and helping to spread the message of Islam. Through their example, they continue to inspire and guide Muslim women to strive for excellence and piety in their own lives, as well as to maintain loving relationships with their husbands and families. Amima represents the ideal of a virtuous and devoted wife and mother and an embodiment of Allah's guidance for husbands and wives in their quest for happiness in this life and in the hereafter.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya, vol. 3, p. 130-131. The name Amima carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ammā bint Ubayd Allah Al-Ansāriyyah was a noblewoman from Banu Umayyah, who had a strong faith in Allah and a great love for the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). She embraced Islam before the migration to Madinah and was one of the first to follow the Prophet during his emigration. She accompanied him in the Battle of the Trench and the Battle of Khaybar.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Baladhuri's Ansab Al-Ashraf, vol. 2, p. 694-695. The name Amima carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ammā bint Ubayd Allah Al-Qurashiyyah was a prominent scholar and religious figure during the early Islamic period. She was known for her piety, knowledge, and generosity, and was a close companion of Imam Ali Zain Al-Abidin (a.s.) and Imam Al-Baqir (a.s.). She played a significant role in the dissemination of knowledge and religious practices during the Umayyad and Abbasid periods.
